mainText: This is Dose of Good for Thursday, November 19. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Public school students win awards for inclusive inventions. Winners of Brazil's Science for All prize include students who built an orthosis that lets people with hand atrophy eat on their own, an electronic cane for deafblind users and a biodigester against energy poverty. Second: Rare insect, possibly a new species, found beside a glacier at the end of the world. On Chile's Navarino Island near Cape Horn, scientists found a stonefly that matches no known species. The find sheds light on life around shrinking glaciers. Third: Project saving Mexico's floating farms wins the 'Nobel of gastronomy'. Lucio Usobiaga won €100,000 for Arca Tierra, a network of 50 farming families keeping Xochimilco's chinampas alive and supplying 60 restaurants. It's the last refuge of wild axolotls. Fourth: Genetic test that spots almost any microbe is now saving lives in hospitals. Metagenomic sequencing identifies every microbe in a sample. In one case it spared a patient a liver transplant; in a London pilot it found causes other tests missed in 30% of cases. Fifth: Corridor map helps jaguars rebound across the Americas. Using GPS data from 172 jaguars in eight countries, scientists mapped 307 core areas and 176 corridors. In Foz do Iguaçu, a jaguar named Tape'ỹ was rescued from a neighbourhood and released in Iguaçu National Park. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
